meta.review_notes: Privacy policy is moderately detailed but leaves several categories unaddressed (contacts, precise location). Terms & Conditions URL returned 404. The AI training opt-out is a notable positive, but the default opt-in for AI training on uploaded photos is a significant concern. Cookie retention of 25 months and data transfer outside EEA are concerning but disclosed.

app.name: PhotoRoom: AI Photo Editor
app.description: An AI-powered photo editor that removes backgrounds, enhances images, and generates professional-quality visuals for e-commerce and social media.

verdict.one_liner: PhotoRoom edits your photos with AI, but may use them to train models unless you opt out, tracks your purchases and device ID for ads, and shares data with multiple service providers.
verdict.summary: PhotoRoom is a capable AI photo editor that requires camera and photo access to function. It offers strong GDPR user rights and claims not to sell your data, but it uses your purchase history and device identifiers for advertising and analytics, stores cookie data for up to 25 months, and may use your uploaded photos to train AI models unless you actively opt out. Data is shared with Apple, RevenueCat, Dub, and other service providers, and may be transferred outside the European Economic Area.
verdict.recommendation_reason: PhotoRoom is useful for photo editing, but your uploaded images may be used to train AI models by default, and the app tracks your purchases and device activity for ads. Turn off AI training in your account settings and avoid uploading sensitive personal photos.

red.title: Your uploaded photos may train AI models by default
red.plain_english: PhotoRoom can use the photos you upload to improve its AI models unless you manually turn this off in your account settings. Once your photos have been used for training, opting out does not undo that past use.

red.title: Your purchases and device ID are tracked for ads
red.plain_english: PhotoRoom uses your purchase history and device identifiers for advertising, analytics, and personalization. The App Store privacy label confirms tracking uses Purchases and Identifiers.

red.title: Cookie data kept for up to 25 months
red.plain_english: Social network and audience measurement cookies store your IP address and pages viewed for up to 25 months with your consent, creating a long-term record of your online activity.

red.title: Data may be transferred outside Europe
red.plain_english: PhotoRoom states that your personal data may be transferred outside the European Economic Area under GDPR protections, which means your data could be stored or processed in countries with different privacy laws.

red.title: Purchase records kept for 10 years
red.plain_english: PhotoRoom retains your purchase and transaction records for a full decade, which is a very long time even by industry standards.

green.title: You can opt out of AI model training
green.plain_english: PhotoRoom allows you to opt out of having your uploaded photos used to train AI models at any time through your account settings.

green.title: Strong GDPR rights including erasure and portability
green.plain_english: PhotoRoom provides extensive user rights under GDPR, including the right to access, delete, and export your data. They typically respond to requests within one month.

green.title: Does not sell or share data for direct ads
green.plain_english: PhotoRoom explicitly states that it does not sell or share your personal information under CCPA definitions, and does not give outsiders your data for their own direct advertising.

green.title: No direct advertising to third parties
green.plain_english: PhotoRoom does not provide your information to outside companies so they can show you ads on other platforms.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom needs access to your camera and photos to edit images, which is the core purpose of the app. Access requires your permission and lasts until you withdraw it.
categories.detail: As a photo editing app, PhotoRoom requires on-demand access to the device camera and photo library. The privacy policy states that device camera and photo access requires approval and lasts until withdrawn. There is no mention of background camera access.
categories.policy_excerpt: Device camera and photo access requires approval and lasts until withdrawn.
concerns: Uploaded photos may be used for AI model training by default

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not mention whether PhotoRoom accesses your GPS location.
categories.detail: No explicit mention of GPS or precise location access in the privacy policy. IP address is collected for cookies and audience measurement, which can reveal approximate location.
categories.policy_excerpt: No explicit mention of GPS or precise location data collection.
concerns: IP address collected for cookies may reveal approximate location

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not mention whether PhotoRoom accesses your contacts or address book.
categories.detail: No reference to contacts, address book, or phonebook access in the privacy policy. The referral program shares addresses with Dub, but this appears to be user-provided referral addresses rather than contact list access.
categories.policy_excerpt: No mention of contacts or phonebook access in the policy.

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom accesses your photos when you choose to upload or edit them. This is required for the app to work, but your uploaded images may be used to train AI models unless you opt out.
categories.detail: Storage access is user-initiated and core to the app's photo editing functionality. The policy notes that uploaded visuals may be used to refine AI models, but users can opt out. API uploads are exempt from AI training use.
categories.policy_excerpt: By operating the service, users acknowledge uploaded visuals may refine AI models, yet they may opt-out of this at any time through account controls.
concerns: Uploaded photos may be used for AI model training by default
Opt-out does not undo prior processing

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom shares your data with service providers like Apple, RevenueCat, and Dub, but claims it does not sell your data or give it to others for their own ads.
categories.detail: Data is shared with technical and hosting service providers, cookie providers (based on banner preferences), Apple and RevenueCat (for refund validation, retained 6 months), Dub (for referral program addresses), and regulators if compelled. The company states it does not sell or share data under CCPA meanings and does not give outsiders information for their own direct ads.
categories.policy_excerpt: Records may be transferred outside the European Economic Area under GDPR protections. We do not 'sell' or 'share' data under CCPA meanings.
concerns: Data transferred outside the EEA
Multiple service providers receive user data
Referral addresses shared with Dub

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom collects your email, login credentials, and purchase records to manage your account. Some data is kept for years even after you stop using the app.
categories.detail: Account data collected includes login credentials, email, and purchase records. Login credentials remain until deletion or 2 years of dormancy, then archived for 5 years. Purchase records are kept for 10 years. Social network and audience measurement cookies preserve IP address and pages viewed for up to 25 months with consent.
categories.policy_excerpt: Gathered details facilitate account management, billing, app operations, support tickets, content moderation, newsletters, and anti-fraud measures.
concerns: Purchase records retained for 10 years
Login credentials archived for 5 years after 2 years dormancy
Cookie data retained for 25 months

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom tracks your purchases and device identifiers for advertising, analytics, and personalization. Cookie data about your online activity is kept for up to 25 months.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label indicates tracking uses Purchases and Identifiers. The privacy policy mentions social network and audience measurement cookies that preserve IP address and pages viewed for up to 25 months with consent. Data is used for advertising, analytics, personalization, and app functionality. User and device IDs, usage details, and crash diagnostics are collected for these purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: Social network and audience measurement Cookies preserve IP address, pages viewed, etc. for up to twenty-five months with consent.
concerns: Purchase history used for advertising and analytics
Device identifiers used for tracking
Cookie data retained for 25 months
Limited opt-out mechanisms mentioned

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom says it is not intended for children under 13, but there is no strong age verification system to enforce this.
categories.detail: The policy states the platform is not intended for children under the age of 13. There is no mention of COPPA compliance, age verification mechanisms, or specific safeguards for children's data beyond the general age restriction.
categories.policy_excerpt: The platform is not intended for...children under the age of 13.
concerns: No robust age verification mechanism
No specific COPPA compliance measures mentioned

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom needs internet access to work. Your IP address is logged and used for cookies and audience measurement, which can reveal what websites you visit.
categories.detail: Internet access is required for the app's AI photo editing features. IP address is collected as part of cookie data for social network and audience measurement purposes, retained up to 25 months. Usage details and crash diagnostics are also collected.
categories.policy_excerpt: Social network and audience measurement Cookies preserve IP address, pages viewed, etc. for up to twenty-five months with consent.
concerns: IP address logged for 25 months via cookies
Usage details and crash diagnostics collected continuously

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom collects your device ID and uses it for advertising and analytics tracking, which helps build a profile of your activity across sessions.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label confirms Identifiers are used for tracking. The privacy policy mentions user and device IDs collected for advertising, analytics, personalization, and app functionality. This constitutes device fingerprinting for ad targeting purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: purchase history, email, photos/videos, user and device IDs, usage details, and crash diagnostics for advertising, analytics, personalization, and app functionality.
concerns: Device IDs used for ad targeting
Identifiers tracked continuously
Creates persistent device profile for analytics

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom does not collect health or biometric data.
categories.detail: No mention of health data, biometric data, or facial recognition data collection in the privacy policy. The app processes photos but does not appear to extract biometric identifiers.
categories.policy_excerpt: No health or biometric data collection described in the policy.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom processes payments through Apple for in-app purchases. It does not store your credit card directly, but keeps your purchase records for 10 years.
categories.detail: Payments are processed through Apple's in-app purchase system. PhotoRoom does not directly handle credit card data. Purchase records are retained for 10 years for accounting and legal purposes. Interaction logs are forwarded to Apple and RevenueCat for refund validation, retained for 6 months.
categories.policy_excerpt: To validate refunds, interaction logs are forwarded to Apple and RevenueCat, where they reside for a six-month term.
concerns: Purchase records retained for 10 years
Interaction logs shared with Apple and RevenueCat

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom gives you GDPR rights to access, delete, and export your data, and they usually respond within a month. However, some data is kept for legal or business reasons even after you request deletion.
categories.detail: Users can exercise rights including access, erasure, data portability, objection to processing, and revocation of consent. Answers typically come within one month, extending to three for complicated issues. However, login credentials remain until deletion or 2 years of dormancy plus 5 years in archives, purchase records are kept for 10 years, and correspondence is held for legal limitation periods.
categories.policy_excerpt: People may exercise extensive controls, including Right of access, Right to erasure/right to be forgotten, Right to data portability, plus options to oppose processing or revoke approval.
concerns: Some data retained for legal/accounting reasons
Long archival periods for dormant accounts
Opt-out of AI training does not undo prior processing

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: PhotoRoom says it will announce updates to the privacy policy, but it is not clear if you will be actively notified or if you need to keep checking the website yourself.
categories.detail: The policy states updates will be announced, but does not specify the mechanism (email, in-app notification, or simply posting to the website). There is no mention of advance notice periods or requiring active re-agreement to material changes.
concerns: Unclear notification mechanism for policy changes
No explicit advance notice period stated
